items.q: Synthetic: a 32 year old woman has resistant hypertension. Angiography shows a beaded mid right renal artery with a normal ostium. The most likely cause is

x.lo: Read a renal angiogram by site and age: mid-artery beads in a young woman point away from atheroma.
x.clues:
- **Young woman** with resistant hypertension
- **Beaded** mid renal artery, ostium normal
- No systemic features of vasculitis
x.ddx:
| Feature | Fibromuscular dysplasia | Atheroma |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Site | Mid artery | Ostium |
| Age | Young | Older |
| Wall | Beaded rings | Eccentric plaque |
x.mechanism: Short fibrous rings alternate with small dilatations in the media, so contrast pools between the rings and the artery looks beaded.
x.key: Fibromuscular dysplasia gives the beaded look because short stenoses alternate with small dilatations in the mid artery.

others.A: Atheroma narrows the origin of the artery in older people with vascular risk factors.
others.C: Polyarteritis nodosa gives small aneurysms and a systemic illness, not smooth mid-artery beads.
others.D: An embolism cuts flow off suddenly, usually with flank pain and a normal downstream wall.

x.pearl: Mid artery beads in a young woman: think fibromuscular dysplasia.
x.rev: Young + mid-artery beads + normal ostium = fibromuscular dysplasia; older + ostial disease = atheroma.

items.q: Synthetic: a 28 year old woman at 26 weeks of gestation has fasting glucose 98 mg/dL twice. The drug that is NOT used for her glycaemic control is

x.clues:
- **Pregnancy** at 26 weeks: organogenesis done, fetal growth phase
- Fasting glucose above the pregnancy target
- The question asks what is **NOT** used
x.mechanism: SGLT2 blockers alter fetal renal development in animal studies and have no safety data in human pregnancy, so they are withheld while insulin, metformin and glyburide have pregnancy experience.
x.key: Empagliflozin is withheld in pregnancy for lack of safety data, while insulin, metformin and glyburide are used.

others.A: Insulin is the standard: it does not cross the placenta in meaningful amounts.
others.B: Metformin crosses the placenta but has wide pregnancy experience and is used.
others.C: Glyburide has pregnancy experience and is used where insulin is not possible.

x.pearl: Newer glucose-lowering classes stay out of pregnancy: no data means do not use.
x.rev: In pregnancy use insulin first, metformin or glyburide when needed; SGLT2 blockers and GLP-1 agents stay out.

items.q: Synthetic: a man cannot extend his wrist after sleeping with his arm over a chair back. Sensation over the first dorsal web space is intact. The site of injury is
o: Axillary nerve in the quadrangular space
Radial nerve in the spiral groove
Posterior interosseous nerve at the arcade of Frohse
Median nerve at the carpal tunnel

x.ddx:
- **Spiral groove**: wrist drop WITH weak brachioradialis and numb first web space
- **Posterior interosseous**: wrist drop with intact sensation and intact brachioradialis
- **Axillary**: deltoid weak, wrist fine
- **Median**: grip and thumb opposition weak, wrist extension fine
x.key: A pure motor wrist drop with intact sensation places the lesion distal to the sensory branch, at the posterior interosseous nerve.

others.A: The axillary nerve supplies the deltoid; a wrist drop rules it out.
others.B: The spiral groove lesion numbs the first web space and weakens brachioradialis; both are intact here.
others.D: The median nerve does not extend the wrist.

x.pearl: Wrist drop with intact feeling: the posterior interosseous branch.

items.q: Synthetic: a trekker is found confused with a core temperature of 29 C and a slow irregular pulse. The next step is
o: Rapid rewarming in a hot bath
Gentle handling, active rewarming and transfer to an ECPR centre
Unrestricted DC shocks until sinus rhythm

x.clues:
- **Core 29 C**: severe hypothermia, confused with an irritable myocardium
- Rough handling can trigger ventricular fibrillation
- Below 30 C drugs and shocks work poorly
x.key: Handle gently, rewarm actively and transfer to an ECPR centre; below 30 C limit shocks to 3 and withhold adrenaline.

others.A: Rapid surface rewarming risks afterdrop and collapse; rewarming is active but controlled.
others.C: Adrenaline is withheld below 30 C because it accumulates and turns toxic on rewarming.
others.D: Shocks are limited to 3 below 30 C; the cold heart rarely converts.

x.pearl: Below 30 C: 3 shocks maximum, no adrenaline, gentle hands.
x.lo: Apply the severe-hypothermia rule: gentle handling, limited shocks, no adrenaline below 30 C.
x.rev: Severe hypothermia: handle gently, rewarm actively, ECPR centre; below 30 C, 3 shocks and no adrenaline.

items.q: Synthetic: a pregnant traveller returns from a Zika outbreak area with a maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis. The fetal risk that guides counselling is

x.lo: Link a maternal viral syndrome to its teratogenic pattern: rash plus red eyes after travel means Zika until proven otherwise.
x.clues:
- **Pregnancy** plus recent travel to an outbreak area
- **Rash with conjunctivitis**: the Zika pair
- Counselling turns on the fetal brain risk
x.ddx:
- **Zika**: rash, conjunctivitis, fetal microcephaly
- **Rubella**: rash with nodes, cataract and deafness
- **CMV**: often silent in the mother, hearing loss in the child
x.mechanism: Zika virus crosses the placenta and infects fetal neural progenitor cells, destroying developing brain tissue.
x.key: Zika in pregnancy threatens the fetal brain, so microcephaly is the counselling point.

others.A: Macrosomia follows maternal diabetes, not Zika.
others.C: Polycythaemia follows chronic fetal hypoxia, not this rash illness.
others.D: Nephrocalcinosis is a calcium disorder, unrelated to Zika.

x.pearl: Rash plus red eyes in pregnancy after travel: think Zika, counsel microcephaly.
x.rev: Zika in pregnancy: rash plus conjunctivitis in the mother, microcephaly in the fetus.

items.q: Synthetic: contrast CT shows a ring-enhancing lesion with smooth thin walls and surrounding oedema in a patient with fever. The most likely diagnosis is

x.mechanism: A bacterial nidus liquefies centrally while a vascular capsule forms around it; contrast leaks from the capsule vessels, giving a smooth thin enhancing ring.
x.key: Fever with a smooth thin-walled ring and oedema is a brain abscess until proven otherwise.

others.A: Glioblastoma gives a thick irregular shaggy ring, usually without fever.
others.C: A subacute infarct follows a vascular territory and does not form a smooth ring.
others.D: A tuberculoma ring is usually thicker with a solid centre and a longer course.

x.pearl: Fever plus a smooth thin ring: brain abscess.

items.q: Synthetic: the first polar body is released
items.exp: The first meiotic division completes just before ovulation, releasing the first polar body.

x.key: Type II pneumocytes make surfactant, which lowers alveolar surface tension.
x.notes:
## Surfactant
- Made by **type II** pneumocytes
- Deficiency causes neonatal respiratory distress

others.A: Type I cells are the thin gas-exchange lining.
